_comment: EVERY number of the simulation lives here. Both editions read this file; if code and this file disagree, this file wins. Values marked (game) are game simplifications; values marked (real) trace to shared/design/sources.json ids. Never change without a CHANGELOG line. Portions generated with the assistance of an SI tool (Claude) and reviewed by Team PlutonyX.

cell._comment: (game) 1 power cell = 10 meter points = 10 kWh. Battery 100 points = 100 kWh.

units._comment: Real-unit conversions shown in Mission Planner view.
units.airNote: (real anchor) 4 crew x 0.84 kg O2 per person per day = 3.36 kg/sol (source: nasa-o2-084). (game) 100 air points = 5 sols of reserve = 16.8 kg.
units.waterNote: (real anchor) about a gallon (3.8 L) per person per day; the ISS recovers about 98 % (source: nasa-water-98). (game) 100 points = 300 L in the loop.
units.solNote: (real) Mars rotates once in about 24.6 hours (source: nasa-mars-facts). (game) one sol is paired with one real UTC day of data.

systems._comment: Index = level 0 Off, 1 Low, 2 Normal, 3 Boost. cost in meter points of power.

cadet.name: Cadet
cadet.blurb: More sunlight, bigger reserves, hints from PIP, no timers.

commander.name: Commander
commander.blurb: Tight margins and a ticking clock in the storm. Learn from failure.

classroom.name: Classroom
classroom.blurb: Cadet numbers, no timers, one class code so everyone flies the same mission, and pause-and-discuss cards.

dust._comment: (game scenario, based on real Mars dust storms; source: jpl-dust-2018). Seeded: start sol and length. Sky per sol of the storm, then one hazy sol, then clear.
dust.dustyPanelsNote: After the storm, panels stay dusty (solar -10) until cleaned by the crew or a dust devil.

radiation._comment: Dose is in micrograys (µGy), the unit of NASA RadLab's MSL-RAD-Surface record. Radiation at these levels never makes a character sick; it fills a dose badge and triggers flight rules.
radiation.habCalmNote: (game) Cosmic rays are very hard to stop; a habitat wall removes only a little.
radiation.habStormNote: (game) Solar storm particles are easier to stop; walls and supplies help.
radiation.cliffNote: (real idea, game number) NASA/JPL: 'Cliffsides or lava tubes would provide additional shielding' (source: jpl-may2024-storm).
radiation.limitsNote: (game) Badge limits are scaled to a 10-sol mission so players can feel the trade-off. Real astronaut limits are far higher and cover a whole career; real crews keep dose 'as low as reasonably achievable'.
radiation.xrayNote: (real) NASA/JPL compared 8,100 µGy to 30 chest X-rays for the 20 May 2024 storm, i.e. 270 µGy each (source: jpl-may2024-storm). Used only for kid-friendly comparisons.

spaceWeather._comment: Rules that turn a real day summary into game values. Implemented in shared/scripts/lib/spaceweather.mjs (deriveGame). Calibration is explained in shared/science-log.md.

calmWindowStorm._comment: If a live window has no storm of level 2+, sols 8 and 9 replay the archived real storm below. The game labels those two sols 'ARCHIVED: real storm of 20 May 2024'.

storm._comment: The storm scene. 1 real second = 1 mission minute on Commander. onsetMinutes is real: on 20 May 2024 the eruption began 05:36 UTC (DONKI) and Curiosity's dose rate peaked about 06:15 UTC (RadLab).
